title: Chapter 215: The Second Apparel
html:
After leaving Director Luo’s office, Chen Ge ate a quick lunch and returned to work. By 6:30 p.m., most park attractions had closed, yet a sizable crowd remained outside the Haunted House.

Visitors gathered beneath the canopy to compare experiences. Those who had survived Mu Yang High School became minor celebrities. Everyone wanted to hear about a two-star scenario, though few dared enter themselves.

The survivors remained pale and drenched in cold sweat, but pride kept them from admitting fear. Instead, they embellished the scenario’s horrors, making the uninitiated even more curious.

After a lengthy discussion, the visitors formed a large team dedicated to conquering the Haunted House. They recorded the precise location of every discovered name tag with almost professional thoroughness. When Chen Ge emerged after closing, their excitement pleased him.

“I hope they find all sixteen name tags soon. The Third Sick Hall has stood empty for too long.”

After cleaning the Haunted House, Chen Ge hurried to Boss Qian’s workshop. Underground, the owner had dragged a chair beside the entrance and sat staring at the mannequins.

“Boss Qian, I came for the mannequins.” Chen Ge touched his shoulder, making the man leap in fright.

“When did you arrive?”

“Just now. What’s wrong? You seem distracted.” Chen Ge entered and applied the finishing touches while Boss Qian stood beside him, watching in silence.

Noticing his odd behavior, Chen Ge probed, “Did something strange happen today?”

Boss Qian’s eyebrows shot up as though Chen Ge had exposed his deepest secret. “How did you know?”

“You were quite obvious about it.”

“Since you’ve discovered the truth, there’s no reason to hide it.” Boss Qian edged closer and whispered mysteriously, “I possess Yin Yang Vision. I can see things others cannot.”

“Yin Yang Vision?” Chen Ge turned to give Boss Qian a once-over. “Have you been watching too many scary movies?”

“It’s true. When I was young, a monk told my father we descended from royalty. Father believed him so completely that he named me Qian Guigen,” Boss Qian explained.

“If you came from royalty, why are you in such a state?”

“Perhaps my destined opportunity hasn’t arrived.” Boss Qian shook his head. “That isn’t important. Today, I saw something unbelievable.”

“Well, what is it?!”

Boss Qian leaned close and whispered, “About four hours ago, this female mannequin winked at me.”

He shielded his mouth with one hand, as if afraid the mannequin might overhear.

“That’s all? Why the female mannequin rather than one of the men?”

“Boss, it blinked! Can you focus on the important part?” Boss Qian seized his arm. “I’m not lying!”

“I didn’t say you were, did I?”

“But you didn’t react when I said I had Yin Yang Vision and saw a mannequin blink!”

“I hear Yin Yang Vision is remarkable. Does it mean you can watch 3D movies without glasses?”

Boss Qian’s mouth fell open. After serious consideration, he finally answered, “No.”

“You’re probably exhausted. Go home and rest. We’ll have plenty of opportunities to work together.” Chen Ge covered the mannequins with white cloth and moved them from the underground workshop.

“Was I really imagining things?” Boss Qian began to doubt himself.

“Don’t worry. Call me if anything happens.” Chen Ge patted his chest reassuringly, then summoned a taxi.

The more Boss Qian considered Chen Ge’s words, the less comforted he felt. Usually, reassurance means saying, “Don’t worry, nothing will happen.” Why did Boss Chen tell me to call if something does?

After hauling the mannequins into the staff break room, Chen Ge’s expression grew serious. He set the white cat among them. Within seconds, it leaped onto the female mannequin and batted at her hair as though tormenting a mouse.

“So something truly is inside.” Chen Ge had not expected the mannequin based on Patient No. 2 to differ from the others. He rested the cleaver against its neck. “I created you, which makes you my responsibility. Obey my instructions and move quietly into your new home.”

His pupils narrowed as fear and anxiety emanated from the mannequin. After considering this, he withdrew the blade. “I was only frightening you. I’m softhearted by nature; I would never hurt any of you deliberately.”

Chen Ge opened the underground entrance and carried the mannequins into the Third Sick Hall. “Welcome. This is your new home.”

He positioned the mannequins throughout the scenario and built several mechanisms around them. Midnight arrived before he finished. Back in the staff break room, he collapsed onto the bed, exhausted after working without rest all day.

Chen Ge checked the black phone’s Daily Missions. The temporary shelter’s completion had already triggered a success notification.

“Congratulations, Specter’s Favored. You have completed a Normal Mission. Terror requires an appropriate recovery period. Considerate service leaves visitors with a favorable impression. Mission reward earned—the Faceless Nurse’s Uniform!

“Faceless Nurse’s Uniform (Costume Prop): Jennie is the wife of Doctor Skull-cracker, Clark. One night, she saw her husband enter a patient’s room carrying an iron mallet. She had no idea what her beloved was doing—until the hammer swung toward her face.”

A Skull-cracker doctor and Faceless Nurse, this is quite a scary story.

Chen Ge put away the phone and slept. Early the next morning, he entered the dressing room. Inside the wooden box that had contained Doctor Skull-cracker’s costume lay a blood-soaked nurse’s uniform.

This is too small for a male mannequin, but it should fit the female mannequin nicely.

Chen Ge inspected the Third Sick Hall. Once satisfied that no hidden safety hazards remained, he opened the Haunted House for business.
